ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows that the probability density function f(x) is piecewise constant: on the central interval [-1,1] the height is a; on the two side intervals [-5,-1] and [1,5] the height is b; outside these intervals it is 0. The figure also marks x=-5,-1,0,1,5, and the central platform height a is higher than the side platform height b. From the normalization condition, the total area is 1: 2a+8b=1. If a 6-level quantizer is to make the output entropy maximum, then the probabilities of the 6 quantization intervals should be equal, all 1/6. The problem gives consecutive decision boundaries as -1, 0, 1, so the intervals [-1,0] and [0,1] each have probability 1/6. Since the density on these two intervals is a and the width is 1, a=1/6. Substituting into 2a+8b=1 gives 2(1/6)+8b=1, therefore b=1/12. Each quantization interval in the two side tails should also have probability 1/6. The tail density is b=1/12, so the required width of each tail quantization interval is (1/6)/(1/12)=2. Therefore the remaining internal decision boundaries are -3 and 3, and the six quantization intervals are [-5,-3], [-3,-1], [-1,0], [0,1], [1,3], [3,5]. The reconstruction levels take the midpoints of the decision boundaries, respectively -4, -2, -0.5, 0.5, 2, 4. The signal power is E[X^2]=∫x^2 f(x)dx. The central part contribution is (1/6)∫_{-1}^{1}x^2dx=1/9; the two side part contribution is (1/12)(∫_{-5}^{-1}x^2dx+∫_{1}^{5}x^2dx)=62/9. Therefore the signal power is 1/9+62/9=7. The quantization noise power is calculated according to midpoint reconstruction for each interval. When a constant-density interval has width Δ, the contribution is density·Δ^3/12. Four tail intervals have width 2 and density 1/12, contributing 4·(1/12)·(2^3/12)=2/9. Two central intervals have width 1 and density 1/6, contributing 2·(1/6)·(1^3/12)=1/36. The total quantization noise power is 2/9+1/36=1/4. So the ratio of signal power to quantization noise power is 7/(1/4)=28.

method.method_draft: Use the image to model f(x)=a on [-1,1], f(x)=b on [-5,-1]∪[1,5], and 0 elsewhere. From normalization, 2a+8b=1. Since the decision boundaries -1, 0, and 1 are consecutive, the cells [-1,0] and [0,1] must each have probability 1/6 under maximum entropy; hence a=1/6 and b=1/12. Each tail cell must also have probability 1/6, so in the tail density b the required width is (1/6)/(1/12)=2, giving remaining internal boundaries -3 and 3. The six reconstruction levels are midpoints: -4, -2, -0.5, 0.5, 2, 4. Compute signal power by integrating x^2 f(x) over the three image-read regions, obtaining 7. Compute quantization noise by summing density*Δ^3/12 over four tail cells of width 2 and two central cells of width 1, obtaining 1/4. Divide to get the ratio 7/(1/4)=28.

所以信号功率与量化噪声功率之比为 7/(1/4)=28。

method.method_draft: Form the CDF implied by the plotted rectangular pdf. Because -1, 0, and 1 are consecutive quantile boundaries, the CDF increments over [-1,0] and [0,1] are each 1/6, so a=1/6. Normalization of the plotted pdf gives 2a+8b=1, hence b=1/12. The CDF then places probability 1/3 to the left of -1 and 1/3 to the right of 1, so the six equiprobable quantile cells are [-5,-3], [-3,-1], [-1,0], [0,1], [1,3], [3,5]. Assign midpoint levels to these cells. Compute E[X^2] by summing c(v^3-u^3)/3 over the six cells, yielding 7. Compute E[(X-Q(X))^2] by summing c[(v^3-u^3)/3-r(v^2-u^2)+r^2(v-u)] for each cell with its midpoint r, yielding 1/4. The signal-to-quantization-noise power ratio is therefore 28.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For six outputs, entropy is maximized by equiprobable quantization cells, so decision boundaries are 1/6-spaced quantiles of the input distribution. For a bin [u,v] with constant density c and reconstruction r=(u+v)/2, use raw moments: signal contribution c(v^3-u^3)/3 and noise contribution c∫_u^v(x-r)^2dx, equivalently c[(v^3-u^3)/3-r(v^2-u^2)+r^2(v-u)].

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像描述：图中 f(x) 是分段矩形概率密度函数，非零支撑从 x=-5 到 x=5；在区间 [-5,-1] 与 [1,5] 上为较低的常数高度 b，在区间 [-1,1] 上为较高的常数高度 a，图上明确标出了 -1、0、1 和两级高度 a、b。推理：6 级量化器要使输出熵最大，因此 6 个量化区间应等概率，各区间概率为 1/6。已知 -1、0、1 是连续判决边界，所以区间 [-1,0] 和 [0,1] 的概率都为 1/6；这两个区间内 pdf 高度为 a、长度为 1，因此 a=1/6。由 pdf 总面积为 1 得 2a+8b=1，代入 a=1/6 得 b=1/12。于是左侧 [-5,-1] 的概率为 4b=1/3，右侧 [1,5] 的概率也为 1/3；每侧需分成两个概率为 1/6 的区间，所以边界为 -5,-3,-1,0,1,3,5。重构电平取各判决边界中点，分别为 -4,-2,-0.5,0.5,2,4。信号功率 E[X^2] 按各段积分 sum c(v^3-u^3)/3 计算，得到 E[X^2]=7。量化噪声功率按各区间中点重构误差积分 sum c[(v^3-u^3)/3-r(v^2-u^2)+r^2(v-u)] 计算，等价于每段 c(v-u)^3/12；四个长度为 2、高度为 b 的外侧小区间贡献 4*(b*8/12)=2/9，两个长度为 1、高度为 a 的中间小区间贡献 2*(a/12)=1/36，总噪声功率为 2/9+1/36=1/4。因此信号功率与量化噪声功率之比为 7/(1/4)=28。

raw_record.original_question: An input to a 6-level quantizer has the probability density function \(f(x)\) as shown in the image. Decision boundaries of the quantizer are chosen to maximize the entropy of the quantizer output. It is given that 3 consecutive decision boundaries are \(-1\), \(0\), and \(1\). Assuming that the reconstruction levels of the quantizer are the mid-points of the decision boundaries, what is the ratio of signal power to quantization noise power?
raw_record.final_cot:
The image shows that the probability density function f(x) is piecewise constant: on the central interval [-1,1] the height is a; on the two side intervals [-5,-1] and [1,5] the height is b; outside these intervals it is 0. The figure also marks x=-5,-1,0,1,5, and the central platform height a is higher than the side platform height b.

From the normalization condition, the total area is 1: 2a+8b=1. If a 6-level quantizer is to make the output entropy maximum, then the probabilities of the 6 quantization intervals should be equal, all 1/6. The problem gives consecutive decision boundaries as -1, 0, 1, so the intervals [-1,0] and [0,1] each have probability 1/6. Since the density on these two intervals is a and the width is 1, a=1/6. Substituting into 2a+8b=1 gives 2(1/6)+8b=1, therefore b=1/12.

Each quantization interval in the two side tails should also have probability 1/6. The tail density is b=1/12, so the required width of each tail quantization interval is (1/6)/(1/12)=2. Therefore the remaining internal decision boundaries are -3 and 3, and the six quantization intervals are [-5,-3], [-3,-1], [-1,0], [0,1], [1,3], [3,5]. The reconstruction levels take the midpoints of the decision boundaries, respectively -4, -2, -0.5, 0.5, 2, 4.

The signal power is E[X^2]=∫x^2 f(x)dx. The central part contribution is (1/6)∫_{-1}^{1}x^2dx=1/9; the two side part contribution is (1/12)(∫_{-5}^{-1}x^2dx+∫_{1}^{5}x^2dx)=62/9. Therefore the signal power is 1/9+62/9=7.

The quantization noise power is calculated according to midpoint reconstruction for each interval. When a constant-density interval has width Δ, the contribution is density·Δ^3/12. Four tail intervals have width 2 and density 1/12, contributing 4·(1/12)·(2^3/12)=2/9. Two central intervals have width 1 and density 1/6, contributing 2·(1/6)·(1^3/12)=1/36. The total quantization noise power is 2/9+1/36=1/4.

So the ratio of signal power to quantization noise power is 7/(1/4)=28.
